references: User-supplied Neo final-approval screenshot and inspected 345-line implementation brief, 2026-08-04
evidence.frequency_or_severity: Three consecutive review corrections exposed a high-severity usability failure: final approval lacked decision-complete, critique-ready context in the conversation.
evidence.current_workaround: Open a 345-line brief and manually reconstruct the product, architecture, and program decisions, interface and contract changes, dependency wiring, call paths, error ownership, slice order, proof strategy, and staged risks.

job: Present a compact, decision-complete final Neo approval request inline while retaining the full implementation brief as a supporting artifact.

rejected_alternatives: Artifact template alone cannot control the interactive approval surface.
A deterministic script cannot reliably select the few consequential decisions.
A repository-wide instruction would apply outside Neo finalization.

positive_triggers: An active Neo finalize-stage handoff has produced a versioned implementation brief.
A changed final-review candidate requires renewed exact-version approval.
negative_triggers: An earlier Neo stage is asking one consequential decision.
A normal non-Neo plan is being summarized.
Implementation or code review has started.
inputs: Approved Neo stage artifacts and decisions
Versioned implementation brief path and SHA-256
Prior review candidate when one exists
outputs: At most 650 words of decision-complete approval context
safe_default: Withhold approval and return to the owning stage when a conflict, blocking unknown, or unclear trade-off prevents an informed decision.
forbidden_effects: Treating an artifact path or hash as the review surface
Inferring approval from silence or clarification
Hiding unresolved blocking risks inside a generic remaining-risks sentence
Recapping every stage or dumping technologies, files, APIs, or low-level pseudocode without a critique-ready structural view
Omitting interface or contract changes, dependency wiring, error ownership, representative flows, or any delivery slice merely to shorten the summary
Rendering structural views as long inline arrow chains, unlabelled blocks, inconsistent indentation, or raw executable code
completion_checks: The approval question is answerable from the conversation without opening the brief.
The summary names critical product, architecture, and program decisions with rationale or trade-off.
The summary shows the external interface and contract delta, distinguishing reused, added, and changed contracts.
The summary renders static dependency wiring and up to three compact concrete runtime paths with transaction ownership and failure or recovery behavior.
Every structural view uses a labelled fenced text block, consistent tree indentation, and one operation per line.
The summary maps important errors or outcomes to their owner and retry, reconciliation, or terminal behavior.
Every delivery slice appears in order with its focused verifier and observable proof.
A boundary-level change surface is present when it materially helps scope review.
The summary names staged residual gates and replan triggers.
The summary stays within the word limit and includes the exact artifact identity.
Approval changes state only after an explicit user response.
